variants.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Edit the attached artwork, which is the exact current icon for AI Tech Review Letters, an independent scholarly and technical review and lecture publication.
Primary request: Turn Q and AI into part of a lively set of SHORT SUBJECT KEYWORDS, rather than a rigid stacked central sub-logo. Add the actual site topics DFT, VQE, LLM, OLED, GPU. Produce one square full-bleed icon artwork, no comparison board or mockup.
Exact text: Render precisely these SEVEN tokens, each ONCE: "Q", "AI", "DFT", "VQE", "LLM", "OLED", "GPU". Use uppercase, correct spelling and well-shaped, separated letters. No long words, fake text, numbers, formulas, extra letters or duplicate tokens. The large structural R already present means Review and is not an additional topic.
Invariants: Keep the recognizable large R formed from folded journal pages, its binding stem and turning upper page, the asymmetrical lower-right watercolor pigment dissolution, dark matte walnut-brown background, parchment-beige paper and restrained desaturated patina-teal details. Preserve a refined original scholarly editorial identity. Artwork remains opaque. Keep dark values and barely perceptible background texture, very restrained surface light; no gold foil, gloss, glitter, 3D bevel, glow, atom orbits, brain, chip, robots or stars.
Typography: Elegant readable editorial serif lettering in parchment-beige or muted teal. Q and AI can be a little larger, but DFT must be clearly readable in the full-size icon. The subject tokens form a gently playful, asymmetrical arrangement with varied scale and a few modest rotations, like scholarly marginalia. Never a rigid vertical list, a balanced grid, a circular seal or a dense word cloud. Give every token breathing room, no overlap or tangencies with the R contours. Keep all meaningful content within an iOS-safe central 80% square. At 180px the tokens should read; at 16px retain the powerful R silhouette. Adjust internal negative space slightly if necessary to accommodate the additional subjects while keeping the overall R immediately recognizable.
Composition A — loose editorial marginalia: use the dark open counter of the upper R for a free, uneven group of Q, AI and DFT, no stacking. Place VQE and LLM in separate breathing pockets adjoining the lower counter and page margins, and OLED and GPU along different parts of the lower open space around the diagonal leg. Place text predominantly in the dark negative spaces, with a couple of small angled annotations lightly following a page edge. The whole composition should feel thoughtfully scattered by a scientific editor, not mechanically centered. Maintain the original tall page-R proportions and generous space.
